pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASS: PREPOSITIONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Which words show direction and time?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify prepositions of time, in, on, at; place in, on, at and direction into, towards, to, through in sentences
2. use prepositions of time, place and direction appropriately for effective communication
3. appreciate the accuracy, appropriateness and correctness of prepositions used in varied texts

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions

Teach
• Focus skill: identify prepositions of time, in, on, at; place in, on, at and direction into, towards, to, through in sentences.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words show direction and time?
2. Why is it important to show time and direction?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
